Corrected invariants: (1) ICE and presence use exclusive/default UDP ownership; Windows enables SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE before bind, and only a fixed-port ownership conflict falls back to a distinct exclusive ephemeral port. Legacy direct and TURN own no sockets; LAN address sharing remains hint-only and has no success callback. (2) Every ICE attempt sends at most five idempotent signed candidate frames at 500 ms intervals inside the 2.5 s tier, stopping automatically on OPEN/cancel/escalation. A candidate generation rotates only for content change or less than eight seconds of expiry headroom; stable content retains generation/credential while issued time advances. (3) local per-target ICE refresh runs netCandidatePlanUpdate, preserves replay entries for same-generation refresh, and clears them only on a credential/generation epoch change; remote same-generation refresh preserves nonce, ACK state, deadline, and probe budget. (4) candidate STUN still uses the bound ICE socket and exact transaction/source demux. Legacy route STUN has no thread, socket bind, or receive path and fails closed until the ENet owner supplies transport-owned demux, preserving D-003 route/candidate separation. (5) a UPnP worker never deletes committed old mappings. Game-thread commit first rejects stale owner unions, then installs the verified result logically, then best-effort removes stale old mappings through saved old-router handles; cancel/failure/mismatch rolls back only new ports. (6) unauthenticated nonce-only TURN is not an openable tier: its compatibility module has no socket/success path and the orchestrator accepts OPEN only from authenticated ICE.

author: claude-week-core-20261114
text: CORE (claude-week-core-20261114), root cause for N-1074 and very likely N-1072 and N-1073, found offline from the ROM and the extracted archives; no game run yet, no repair yet. The scene extractor drops whole rooms. s_buildBgVisualExports (port/src/romextract_pdarena.c) sizes each room's work buffer from the room's COMPRESSED length (room_span * 8 + 4096, minimum 65536) and then skips the room, silently, when its inflated length exceeds an eighth of that buffer. So every room whose display data inflates to more than 8192 bytes (or more than its compressed size plus 512) is left out of scene.glb. The guard dates from the first version of the export (cd57ca2b, 2026-05-21). Measured against the ROM for every background file: Defection and Extraction lose 14 of 167 rooms holding 10,479 of 19,780 triangles (53.0 percent; rooms 2, 57, 128 to 133 and 162 to 167, the last six being the largest in the stage); Attack Ship 64.4 percent, Air Force One 53.5, Crash Site 46.5, Pelagic II 44.8, Investigation 42.1, Deep Sea 36.0, Air Base 32.8, Area 51 25.8, Villa 24.1, Skedar Ruins 23.7, Chicago 18.8, Carrington Institute and Defense 16.5 (5 rooms), G5 10.3; four multiplayer arenas lose one or two rooms each. The 153 Defection rooms that are exported match the ROM triangle for triangle, and the scene's 9,301 triangles are exactly the kept ones. Collision, room bounds, portals and navigation come from other tables and are complete, which is why play works and floors look missing. The same extractor records no cull mode: the room display lists set and clear G_CULL_BACK (on Defection the original draws 92.5 percent of the triangles with back faces culled and 7.5 percent two-sided), and the scene renderer draws everything two-sided. Next from me: the fix on a new branch (buffer from the rzip header's inflated size, a skipped room becomes an extraction error instead of a silent continue, cull mode carried per material as glTF doubleSided and honoured by the renderer), a check of every scene against the ROM room by room, a re-extraction and shared base, then captures of the Defection intro, Defection rooms and the Carrington Institute computers before and after. Evidence scripts (read-only, my scratchpad): vis/room_skip_check.py, vis/room_dl_census.py, vis/scene_rooms.py.

author: claude-week-core-20261114
text: CORE (claude-week-core-20261114), cause for N-1073 (the Carrington Institute computer face), read from the code, the extracted archives and the Grid session's capture ci-motion-c.png of 2026-11-18; fix written on week-pd/core-s11, not yet run in the game. It is a prop's screen, not room geometry: the Institute's scene has no animated monitor material and its 8 single_monitor objects use base:model_goodpc. tvscreenRender (src/game/propobj.c) copies the screen node's vertices 0 to 3 as the screen's four corners and draws triangles (0,1,2) and (0,2,3). A model compiled from typed source stores each node's triangles flattened, three vertices each (port/src/modasset_compiler.c, fillGeneratedTriVertices), so the screen node's six vertices are A B C A C D and vertex 3 is A again: the second triangle has no area, and that half of the screen shows the casing behind it. The capture shows exactly this: the screen's text covers one triangle, split along the diagonal. All 15 screen nodes of the 12 base monitor models are one load of four vertices drawn as (0,1,2), (0,2,3), so every monitor and TV screen in the game is affected (235 monitor objects in the base scenarios: PCs, terminals, TV screens, comms hubs, consoles, the G5 alarm and laser switches). Bug B-1290. The fix reads vertex 5 as the fourth corner when the node has six vertices whose fourth and fifth repeat the first and third. The desk and monitor artifacts N-1010 left open are probably this. So the three reports have three causes on my side: Defection's missing floors and walls and its empty intro are B-1266 (rooms left out of every scene), the flipped-looking surfaces are B-1266 with B-1267 (no cull mode) and perhaps B-1268 (reflective surfaces, open), and the computer face is B-1290.
